name: Equity Across Schools
title: Equity Across Schools
answer: Equity across schools means making sure AI adoption does not widen the gap between well-resourced schools and those serving students with the greatest needs. District leaders should direct coaching, champions, training, and devices to the schools that need them most, and check pilot results across all schools rather than in aggregate. It matters because the goal is for every school to benefit, not just the ones already ahead.

sections.body: AI adoption can widen gaps between schools because schools with more resources, stronger leadership, and more tech savvy staff tend to adopt tools faster and use them better, while schools serving students with the greatest needs may fall behind. This idea asks district leaders to watch for that pattern and to intervene deliberately. It solves the problem of an uneven rollout that quietly increases inequality between schools. It also extends the concern beyond whether AI is used at all to how it is used. The aim is that every school benefits from AI, not only those that were already ahead.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: Districts put this into practice by directing support where it is needed most, targeting coaching, champions, training, and devices to the schools that need them. When pilots are run, leaders check the results across schools rather than only in aggregate, so that a strong average does not hide weak results in particular schools. Leaders also examine how AI is used in each school, not just whether it is used. If students in some schools use AI for creative projects and deep inquiry while students elsewhere use it only for drill, the learning gap grows. The same high expectations should apply everywhere, so no school is left with a thinner version of the work.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or formal evidence label for this idea. It presents equity across schools as a pattern district leaders should watch for and a set of actions they should take, rather than as a finding backed by research. This idea therefore rests on practice and professional judgment rather than on research evidence as stated in the book.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets the limits in terms of risks and decisions that stay with people. The main risk is that AI adoption widens gaps between schools, with better-resourced schools moving faster and schools serving students with the greatest needs falling behind. A second risk is a gap in how AI is used, where some students get creative projects and deep inquiry while others get only drill. District leaders carry the responsibility to watch for these patterns, to target support where it is needed most, and to check pilot results across schools rather than in aggregate. The decisions about where support goes and what counts as good use remain with people, and the same high expectations should apply everywhere.
